commits.message:
feat(reporting): add Recruitment and Sender Intelligence reports (P1)

Completes the two P1 reports from the report spec: Recruitment Data
Intelligence ("turns ingestion into Jobfynder market intelligence")
and Sender Intelligence ("begins building recruiter/company
relationship intelligence"), replacing their ComingSoon placeholders
in the Reports dashboard.

Schema investigation before writing anything, same as every other
report this session: confirmed skill_usage_stats holds cumulative
all-time skill counts (no per-day breakdown -- top_skills is
documented as all-time, not windowed by `days`), confirmed
normalized_job_titles/normalized_skills are stored as jsonb (not a
Postgres array -- unnest() doesn't apply, needed
jsonb_array_elements_text() instead, caught by the test suite before
it shipped a 500), confirmed job_requirement records carry location/
employment_type/work_authorization/rate_or_salary as free text, and
confirmed metadata.exact_content_duplicate_of (set in
app/channels/service.py at intake time) is the real, existing
duplicate-detection signal to reuse rather than inventing a new
definition of "duplicate" for this report.

Bug caught while investigating, fixed before it reached the new
report: skill_usage_stats' top entry by times_seen was "https" at
~4,950 occurrences -- a URL-scheme fragment that got approved as a
taxonomy candidate before the noise filter (_is_noise_skill_term,
added earlier this session for the daily triage job) existed. Several
other entries in the top 30 were the same class of contamination
(issues, process, governance, Perform, Deliver, Ensure, Troubleshoot).
Rather than editing the canonical taxonomy file (out of scope here,
and risky -- other systems read it), get_recruitment_intelligence's
top_skills now filters every result through the same
_is_noise_skill_term() check the daily triage job already uses, so
the report shows real skills instead of taxonomy contamination.
Covered by a regression test.

New app/reporting/service.py functions, same read-only contract as
every other report:
- get_recruitment_intelligence(days, limit): top skills (all-time,
  noise-filtered), top job titles, top locations, employment types,
  work authorization, and rate/salary-specified rate, all from actual
  job_requirement records.
- get_sender_intelligence(days, limit): top senders and sender domains
  by draft volume, jobs-vs-hotlists split, average parse confidence,
  and exact-content-duplicate rate per sender/domain.

Both wired into GET /reports/overview, new GET /reports/recruitment-
intelligence and GET /reports/sender-intelligence endpoints, and the
assistant's tool registry -- so a chat question about top skills,
which senders send the most, or duplicate postings is answered from
the exact same functions the dashboard renders.

Frontend: new RankedList (horizontal-bar ranked list, used for skills/
titles/locations/employment-types/work-authorization) and SenderTable
components in ReportsPage.tsx. Recruitment Intelligence and Sender
Intelligence tabs now render real data instead of "isn't built yet."
Data Quality Exceptions and Claim & Publish Funnel remain honest
ComingSoon placeholders -- not requested yet.

6 new checks in scripts/hermes-950-reporting-assistant-check.py:
shape tests for both new functions, the noise-filter regression test
(top_skills must never include "https"), a jobs+hotlists+other-sums-
to-total invariant for sender entries, dashboard-overview coverage,
and both new endpoints via the real FastAPI app. Full regression
suite run against a fresh schema and freshly built image:
hermes-950-reporting-assistant-check.py passes all 26 checks. Ran
every other hermes-*.py script in the suite against the same fresh
schema -- failures reproduce identically to prior runs this session
(mailbox routing, MS Graph credentials, live-server dependencies --
none touch app/reporting, app/assistant, or app/routers/reporting.py).
Frontend type-checks and builds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
